papers.title: Hyper Association Graph Matching with Uncertainty Quantification for Coronary Artery Semantic Labeling
papers.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is one of the primary causes leading to death worldwide. Accurate extraction of individual arterial branches on invasive coronary angiograms (ICA) is important for stenosis detection and CAD diagnosis. However, deep learning-based models face challenges in generating semantic segmentation for coronary arteries due to the morphological similarity among different types of coronary arteries. To address this challenge, we propose an innovative approach using the hyper association graph-matching neural network with uncertainty quantification (HAGMN-UQ) for coronary artery semantic labeling on ICAs. The graph-matching procedure maps the arterial branches between two individual graphs, so that the unlabeled arterial segments are classified by the labeled segments, and the coronary artery semantic labeling is achieved. By incorporating the anatomical structural loss and uncertainty, our model achieved an accuracy of 0.9345 for coronary artery semantic labeling with a fast inference speed, leading to an effective and efficient prediction in real-time clinical decision-making scenarios.

summary_en.motivation: To address challenges in semantic segmentation of coronary arteries due to morphological similarity among different artery types.
summary_en.method: Proposes a hyper association graph-matching neural network with uncertainty quantification for mapping arterial branches between graphs.
summary_en.result: Achieves an accuracy of 0.9345 for coronary artery semantic labeling with fast inference speed.
summary_en.validation: Validated on clinical invasive coronary angiogram datasets, demonstrating effectiveness for real-time decision-making.

papers.title: Adaptive Uncertainty-Guided Model Selection for Data-Driven PDE Discovery
papers.abstract: We propose a new parameter-adaptive uncertainty-penalized Bayesian information criterion (UBIC) to prioritize the parsimonious partial differential equation (PDE) that sufficiently governs noisy spatial-temporal observed data with few reliable terms. Since the naive use of the BIC for model selection has been known to yield an undesirable overfitted PDE, the UBIC penalizes the found PDE not only by its complexity but also the quantified uncertainty, derived from the model supports' coefficient of variation in a probabilistic view. We also introduce physics-informed neural network learning as a simulation-based approach to further validate the selected PDE flexibly against the other discovered PDE. Numerical results affirm the successful application of the UBIC in identifying the true governing PDE. Additionally, we reveal an interesting effect of denoising the observed data on improving the trade-off between the BIC score and model complexity. Code is available at https://github.com/Pongpisit-Thanasutives/UBIC.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要关注数据驱动偏微分方程发现中的不确定性量化模型选择，不涉及仿真采样效率或植入物设计优化。
llm.why_not_core: Does not address simulation sampling efficiency, does not handle constraints in optimization, and is not validated on biomechanics or implant design problems.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有BIC准则在含噪数据中发现偏微分方程时易过拟合，需要不确定性感知的模型选择方法。
summary_zh.method: 提出不确定性惩罚的贝叶斯信息准则UBIC，结合物理信息神经网络进行验证。
summary_zh.result: UBIC成功识别出真实控制方程，且去噪可改善BIC分数与模型复杂度的权衡。
summary_zh.validation: 通过多个数值基准案例验证了方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: The naive use of BIC for model selection in PDE discovery often leads to overfitted equations; an uncertainty-aware approach is needed.
summary_en.method: An uncertainty-penalized Bayesian information criterion (UBIC) is proposed, utilizing coefficient of variation from probabilistic model supports, and physics-informed neural network learning for flexible validation.
summary_en.result: UBIC successfully identifies the true governing PDE from noisy data, and denoising improves the trade-off between BIC score and model complexity.
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of UBIC in discovering the correct PDE.

papers.title: Effect of boron element on microstructure and mechanical properties of 316L stainless steel manufactured by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Boron(B)element is often utilized to enhance mechanical properties of stainless steel due to its excellent performance. In this study, selective laser melting (SLM) was used to print 316L/B stainless steel with varying boron weight content. The effects of boron content on microstructure, nanoindentation, and mechanical properties of the printed 316L stainless steel were discussed. Fine cell dendrites and columnar crystals were found in the SLM printed stainless steel due to the rapid solidification in SLM. It was found that boron has a higher growth limiting factor in the iron system and the boron solute can provide a high component supercooling. By adding boron element to stainless steel during printing, the honeycomb and grain size after solidification are significantly reduced due to interactions between the boron element and the 316L.Tensile testing results show that the ultimate tensile strength of the SLM fabricated parts with 0.5wt% and 1wt% boron element addition can be increased significantly to 1071 MPa and 1174 MPa, respectively.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了硼元素对选区激光熔化316L不锈钢微观结构和力学性能的影响，但未涉及生物医学植入物相关的应力遮挡、疲劳或骨整合等关键问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on enhancing tensile strength via boron addition in 316L steel by SLM, but does not address porous structure, stress shielding, fatigue testing, surface roughness, or osseointegration relevant to biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过添加硼元素提高SLM成形316L不锈钢的力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM制备不同硼含量的316L/B不锈钢，进行微观结构和拉伸测试。
summary_zh.result: 添加0.5wt%和1wt%硼使抗拉强度显著提高至1071 MPa和1174 MPa。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸试验验证力学性能提升。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the mechanical properties of 316L stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting through boron addition.
summary_en.method: 316L stainless steel with varying boron content (0.5wt% and 1wt%) was processed by SLM, followed by microstructural characterization and tensile testing.
summary_en.result: The ultimate tensile strength increased significantly to 1071 MPa and 1174 MPa with 0.5wt% and 1wt% boron, respectively.
summary_en.validation: The mechanical property improvement was validated by standard tensile tests.
